sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of federal mail fraud statutes regarding public officials. the side that brought the case argues the law requires a specific quid pro quo. The government contends that hiding a conflict of interest violates the statute. The Court must define the boundary between these two legal standards.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the criminal liability of public officials who hide conflicts of interest. It clarifies the scope of federal mail fraud laws. It impacts how prosecutors charge officials for nondisclosure. It sets a national standard for defining fraud in public service.
